messages:
alex_w: Heads-up — prod inference cluster showed recurring p99 tail spikes during the 12:00–14:00 UTC window. Concurrency ~1200, steady QPS. p50/p95/p99 went from 18/55/120ms to 22/90/410ms.
nina_ml: yikes. any smoking gun yet? :eyes:
alex_w: preliminary flamegraphs point to lots of time in the slow kernel path that we only hit after KV cache misses / eviction churn. Looks like eviction + microbatch coalescing boundary causes a cascade.
jon: can you paste the profile and the kernel selection trace? curious whether it's the attention kernel or the matmul fallback.
alex_w: sure — grabbed a capture during a spike. snippet:

```
# perf snapshot
runtime: kernel_select -> fallback_slow_kernel (40%)
serving: kv_get -> miss -> eviction_writeback stalls (25%)
batched_send: microbatch_wait -> merge_cost (15%)
```

Also ran a short experiment toggling microbatch_size: 8 -> p99 410ms, 4 -> p99 220ms, 16 -> p99 760ms. throughput dropped ~12% at mb=4 vs mb=8.
maria_r: that aligns with the microbatch SLO tradeoff: smaller mb reduces queueing latency and contention but hurts throughput and GPU utilization.
nate_infra: any sign of lock contention in the KV shard? we had a mutex hotpath in the eviction path last year.
alex_w: yes — there are bursts where eviction walker holds the shard lock and the cache-miss path serializes. When that happens, kernel selection sees more short sequences (no KV prefix) and selects a slower kernel due to different seq-len heuristics. Combined effect: eviction stalls -> more misses -> slower kernel -> longer tokens -> longer KV pressure.
nina_ml: so a feedback loop. thoughts on mitigations?
jon: short list:
- adaptive microbatching: shrink mb when hotset churn detected (react faster than static config)
- prioritize KV eviction IO off the critical path (async writeback + softer shard locking)
- force kernel bias: prefer fast kernel for first N tokens after miss to avoid fallback, at cost of slightly higher compute
- bump per-worker cache quota to reduce eviction frequency for hot endpoints

alex_w: tested quick patch to bias kernel selection for newly-miss requests. p99 improved from 410ms -> 270ms at mb=8, throughput drop negligible. Patch is in branch: `fix/evict-kernel-bias`.
deploy-bot: perf-ci run started — https://ci.internal/runs/8842 :spinner:
maria_r: nice. longer term we should quantify unit-cost change. smaller mb reduced p99 but increased cost by ~11% in tokens/GPU efficiency.
nate_infra: I'll prototype an async eviction queue that uses lock-free ring for writeback. should cut hold-time on the eviction walker.
alex_w: proposal: short-term deploy kernel-bias + enable adaptive microbatch alpha flag for specific customer pool. medium-term: async eviction + adaptive mb policy that watches kv_miss_rate and p95.
nina_ml: agree. schedule a canary for low-risk tenant group and run the 24hr perf harness.
jon: add a regression test to perf CI that recreates the eviction storm pattern (concurrency ramp + hot key churn). if that fails we block merges.
alex_w: created an issue with checklist and numbers: https://tickets.internal/INF-1724
maria_r: ok thumbs-up from PMs? :thumbsup:
alex_w: PMs looped in, they care about tail more than 3% throughput delta for these endpoints. deploying kernel-bias to canary now.
nate_infra: will follow up with a prototype PR for async eviction later today.
alex_w: thanks all — will update after canary results. :rocket:
